status: Qualified native lifecycle observations; not helper-route or BizHawk transport acceptance
scope: Shipping payload, original retail startup rooms and positions, existing post-tutorial native file 0.
Experimental Phone config enabled before boot, synthetic authentication identity and complete item history; no live AP server.
Ability gating ON, health minimum 6 and maximum 10, Area Keys ON, unchanged finite Sir Kibble Cutter source.
The actual guarded Phone queue grants ownership after native Cutter acquisition; no pose, equipment, HP, battery, room or CPU-state writes.
Earlier approach takes native damage from HP 6 to 5; this is not minimum-health or damage-free route evidence.
Snapshots are checkpoint observations, not a per-frame trace.

Historical write-origin labels production-mailbox-four-item-history refer to the three initial receipts (East Hub, Moonlight Key, Cutter); Phone is appended later and granted through its separate queue.
findings: Three eligible calls in 143, 801 and 190 naturally exhaust batteries 3 to 2 to 1 to 0.
At zero battery L still returns from 190 to 801 and ordinary movement works.
With all three CPUs still in 190, a subsequent 60-frame R hold in 801 does not spend or start a call at the recorded checkpoint; Phone remains owned.

An offline cold reload of the resulting native save preserves Phone ownership, refills batteries to 3 and recreates all four Kirbys with Normal in 801. No client reads or writes are invoked by the offline harness.
A separate offline reload of that same saved file under a different synthetic ROM identity invalidates ownership and retains native control.

An eight-frame R press enters native startup; releasing R for one frame and holding L for 120 does not cancel the pending call. It consumes one battery, brings all CPUs to 143, and a later L returns to 801 with movement restored.
limits: Only native file 0 is exercised here; cross-file acceptance and broader ability/state coverage remain open.
No arbitrary source assignment, new helper traversal, solo alternative, RoomSanity behavior or runtime multiplayer guarantee follows.
The native mGBA bridge is not the BizHawk Lua transport.
A one-frame exploratory R press did not enter a call; the eight-frame trial does not establish a minimum press duration or general interruption behavior.
